krs.name: 1.1 · Ad batches ready within 5 working days
krs.metric: Standard batches (4 concepts × 2 hooks) ready to launch within 5 working days of release, out of the 8 released from Nov 2 to Dec 21
krs.source: Fibery tickets: release and ready timestamps · read by Michael before each weekly review
krs.lead: Batch released every Monday from the footage bank

inits.name: Bank and release
inits.hyp: If we shoot in bulk into a footage bank (about one shoot day a month) and release one standard batch from it every Monday, then batches are ready within 5 working days
inits.contrib: Takes the shoot out of the weekly clock

inits.name: Michael out of the middle
inits.hyp: If briefs come from the briefing engine, the editor owns engineering QC and Michael only approves scripts and final cuts, then batches stop waiting in his queue

miles.text: Checkpoint · release standard and timestamps live
M1 · Batch 02 ready: 4 concepts × 2 hooks released from the footage bank Oct 26, launch kit complete, every handoff logged (shared with KR 1.2)
Checkpoint · at least 2 of the last 3 batches ready within 5 working days
M2 · Batch released Nov 30 ready by Dec 4, with Michael only on script and final-cut approval
Target · at least 7 of 8 batches ready on time, no week missed

risks.text: Engineering is a single point of failure: one engineer, one render machine (down twice on Oct 13)
risks.fix: Two late batches in a row because of engineering: decide a second render capacity at the next weekly review

risks.text: No batch released by Monday noon
risks.fix: Raise the cause the same day, not at the Saturday review

risks.text: Footage bank below two weeks of concepts
risks.fix: Book the next shoot day that week

krs.name: 1.2 · Handoffs accepted on first submission
krs.metric: Share of ads accepted the first time at the shooting → engineering and engineering → editing handoffs, Nov 2 to Dec 27, per ad
krs.source: Fibery tickets: pass or fail per ad with defect type, logged by the receiver · read by Michael
krs.lead: Failures on items already on the checklists

inits.name: Fix the root cause in engineering
inits.hyp: If the custom chunker goes into the pipeline and Ilya runs a listening pass before handing over, then first-pass acceptance from engineering rises from about 2 in 3 to 90% or more

inits.name: The receiver defines done
inits.hyp: If each receiving team writes its checklist and the sender runs it before submitting, then failures from missing items disappear
inits.contrib: Removes access, reference and segment-map failures

miles.text: Checkpoint · both checklists signed, per-ad handoff log live
M1 · every Batch 02 handoff judged against the two signed checklists and logged per ad with its defect type (shared with KR 1.1)
M2 · chunker and listening pass live: at least 15 of 16 ads from engineering pass first time over two consecutive batches
Checkpoint · at least 80% over the trailing four weeks
Target · at least 90% over the window

risks.text: Chunker not live by Nov 8
risks.fix: Milestone 2 moves and the gap is logged

risks.text: Receivers absorb rework: more than 3 passes with a note in a week
risks.fix: Review the checklist

risks.text: 3 or more failures at the same boundary in a batch
risks.fix: The sender presents the root cause at the next weekly review

krs.name: 1.3 · 70% of new students reach a first result in 30 days
krs.metric: Share of students joining from Nov 1 who reach their validated first concrete result within 30 days of access (refunded students stay in the count)
krs.source: Data OS: status per step updated by the CSM, result validated by the coach or the CSM · checked by Romain
krs.lead: Share of new students who completed the day-7 step

inits.name: Clarity
inits.hyp: If every new student knows from day one what their first result is and follows a 30-day path with dated steps, then at least 70% reach it within 30 days

inits.name: Early rescue
inits.hyp: If every student is tracked at every step and an alert fires when one falls behind, then a coach or the CSM steps in within 24 hours and brings most at-risk students back

miles.text: M1 · first concrete result defined with proof criteria, 30-day path (day 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 30) live in the Data OS, every current student set up (week to schedule, live before Nov 1)
M2 · every student tracked at every step, rescue alert with a coach or the CSM contacting within 24 h (week to schedule, live before Nov 1, shared with KR 3.3)
Target · November cohort at or above 70% (final end of December), December cohort confirmed end of January

risks.text: November cohort below 40% at mid-December
risks.fix: Redesigning the 30-day path becomes the first priority

risks.text: Alerts exceed what the coach and the CSM can handle within 24 hours
risks.fix: Escalate capacity at the next weekly review, before any increase in enrollment

risks.text: Delivery load reaches 90% of capacity
risks.fix: Adjust the enrollment pace: student results come first

krs.name: 2.1 · 5 qualified live calls per day per sales rep
krs.metric: Qualified first sales calls held in December ÷ rep-working-days in December (all four qualification criteria confirmed by the sales rep)
krs.source: Data OS: every call tagged held or no-show, qualified or not, the day it happens · checked by Amin
krs.lead: Share of held calls that are qualified, and show rate, per VSL

inits.name: The VSL archetype
inits.hyp: If the VSL speaks to people who already carry part of the identity of an interior designer, then more of the people who book are qualified and more of them show up
inits.contrib: Qualified share and show rate up

inits.name: The gate before the calendar
inits.hyp: If the setter checks every application against the four criteria and every booked call gets a confirmation and reminder sequence, then unqualified prospects stop reaching the sales rep

miles.text: M1 · four qualification criteria validated by Michael, Liam and Valentino; every call of the week tagged held or no-show, qualified or not, in the Data OS (week to schedule, in October)
M2 · the two new VSLs on the interior-designer-identity archetype take 100% of guru #1 traffic, show rate and qualified share compared with the old VSL (week to schedule, by mid-November)
Target · December average at or above 5 qualified live calls per day per sales rep

risks.text: Fewer than half of held calls qualified two weeks after the new VSLs
risks.fix: Next VSL iteration becomes the first priority, setter gate starts the following week

risks.text: Show rate still below 50% at the end of November
risks.fix: Start the reminder flow

risks.text: Last two weeks of November below 4 qualified calls a day
risks.fix: Review the December plan the following Saturday

risks.text: Cost per qualified live call above $500 (KR 2.2; $500 = $125 per booked call at 50% show and 50% qualified)
risks.fix: Stop scaling spend until it is back at or under $500

krs.name: 2.2 · Cost per qualified live call ≤ $500
krs.metric: Meta spend over the trailing 28 days ÷ qualified first calls held from paid bookings in the same 28 days (baseline is a provisional estimate until the October rebuild)
krs.source: Sales source of truth (one record per booked call, joined to ad spend) · read every Sunday, spot-checked by Romain
krs.lead: Drivers: cost per booked call ≤ $125, show rate ≥ 50%, qualified share ≥ 50%

inits.name: The VSL of KR 2.1
inits.hyp: If the VSL speaks to the interior-designer identity and frames the investment before booking, then the qualified share rises from 1 in 3 to 1 in 2 and the show rate from 40% to 50%

inits.name: Ads that filter, powered by the AD ENGINE
inits.hyp: If every ad speaks to the buyer archetype and the budget moves each week to the ads with the lowest cost per qualified live call, then the booking cost falls toward $125 while the qualified share rises

inits.name: Teach Meta what a good booking is
inits.hyp: If Meta receives an event each time a booking passes the application and the setter check, then an ad set optimized on it brings a lower cost per qualified live call

miles.text: New VSL and CHAIR ads live, every booking carries its VSL version and ad ID
M1 · sales source of truth live with October in it; measured baseline and its three drivers published, one figure recomputed by Romain
AD ENGINE v1 · bookings, shows and qualified calls per ad, at least 90% of qualified calls matched to an ad
M2 · budget steered on cost per qualified live call, reallocation approved by Amin · checkpoint ≤ $800 trailing 28 days
Qualified-booking event fired reliably for two weeks, optimized test ad set live
Verdict on bet 3 after $2,000 of spend, winner scaled
Independent audit · Romain checks 20 records against the recordings, no discrepancy left open
Target · ≤ $500 over the trailing 28 days, reproduced by Romain

risks.text: October baseline above $1,500
risks.fix: Partners decide whether $500 by December is still realistic before more budget is committed

risks.text: Trailing cost above $800 at W47
risks.fix: Stop scaling spend; W48 to W50 go to the weakest driver with its owner

risks.text: Fewer than 95% of a week’s bookings recorded
risks.fix: Mark the scorecard provisional; Amin brings the cause to the weekly review

risks.text: Closing rate below 35% for four weeks
risks.fix: Re-cut the target ($450 at 30%)

krs.name: 2.3 · Trust score ≥ 8/10, prospects and sales team
krs.metric: Lower of the two December scores out of 10: external (1 − share of qualified calls whose main objection is trust in guru #1 or in the promise) × 10, and internal (Friday pulse of the sales team)
krs.source: Data OS: main objection tagged on every qualified call, Friday pulse · Amin checks five recordings a week
krs.lead: Share of calls tagged trust in guru #1 or trust in the promise

inits.name: Her real work, captured
inits.hyp: If prospects see guru #1 at work (clips from her coaching sessions, with consent) and her track record as a designer, then doubt about her stops being the main objection

inits.name: A promise we can prove
inits.hyp: If we lead with the first concrete result students reach within 30 days (KR 1.3), backed by real student stories, then trust in the promise rises for prospects and for the sales team

miles.text: M1 · objection list validated by Amin and Valentino, 100% of the week’s qualified calls tagged, first Friday pulse answered by every sales rep (week to schedule, in October)
M2 · "Who she is" page with track record and three consented clips sent to 100% of booked prospects, trust-in-guru share compared with the two weeks before (week to schedule, by mid-November)
Target · each December score at or above 8/10

risks.text: Trust is the main objection on more than 40% of calls at the end of November
risks.fix: First priority of the marketing review

risks.text: Internal score below 7 two weeks in a row
risks.fix: Amin meets the sales team and Romain to check that what we advertise matches what students get

risks.text: Internal score two points below the external one
risks.fix: Review the promise before the next ad goes live (KR 3.3)

krs.name: 3.1 · $200k cash collected in December
krs.metric: Payments for guru #1’s offers received between Dec 1 and Dec 31 (in full, instalments, BNPL payouts at full price), minus refunds paid in the same period
krs.source: Stripe and BNPL statements, reconciled weekly in the Data OS by Amin
krs.lead: Share of yeses paid within 24 hours

inits.name: Paid on the call
inits.hyp: If every yes is paid before the call ends, in full or through a BNPL application completed with the sales rep on screen, then the gap between sales and cash closes

inits.name: Undecided into decided
inits.hyp: If every qualified prospect who needs time leaves with a follow-up within 72 hours, and each month closes with an official incentive (December: Friday Dec 18), then more of them buy

inits.name: Down-sell for BNPL declines (in reserve)
inits.hyp: If declines still cost more than a third of yeses once a second BNPL provider is live, then a lighter upfront offer turns paid-for calls into cash

miles.text: M1 · cash view live in the Data OS: every payment since Oct 1 by day and type, reconciled with Stripe and BNPL, October reconciled to the dollar (week to schedule, in October)
M2 · payment step written into every call, 100% of the week’s yeses go through it, share paid within 24 hours logged (week to schedule, by mid-November)
Half of the target ($100k) collected by Dec 15
Target · December cash at or above $200k, final in the first week of January

risks.text: More than a third of BNPL applications declined
risks.fix: Signing a second provider for lower credit profiles becomes the first priority

risks.text: Less than $100k collected by Dec 15
risks.fix: Follow-up pipeline becomes the first priority, never a discount

risks.text: Fewer than 80% of a week’s yeses paid within 24 hours
risks.fix: Review the payment step the same week

risks.text: December needs about 115 qualified calls: about $57k of ads at $500 per qualified live call (KR 2.2), not the ~$35k first planned
risks.fix: Budget December ads on $500 per qualified live call; keeps cost per sale at or under $1,500 at the 35% close rate (KR 3.2)

krs.name: 3.2 · Close 35% of qualified live calls
krs.metric: Qualified first calls held in December that became a paid sale within 14 days ÷ qualified first calls held in December (qualification locked before the outcome)
krs.source: Data OS and CRM, every call recorded · read by Valentino before each weekly review; any change of qualification arbitrated by Amin after listening to the recording
krs.lead: Lost qualified calls reviewed against the call structure

inits.name: A written call structure
inits.hyp: If every call follows a structure built from Valentino’s best won calls and two lost qualified calls are reviewed against it every week, then the rate rises

inits.name: Answer the real objections
inits.hyp: If the two most frequent objections on lost qualified calls each get a tested answer and its proof, then the sales rep stops losing the same sale twice

miles.text: M1 · qualification recorded before every call and confirmed in its first ten minutes, every qualified call shows its outcome in the Data OS (week to schedule, in October, shared with KR 2.1 M1)
M2 · call structure v1 written from ten won calls and validated by Valentino, used on 100% of qualified calls, first two lost calls reviewed (week to schedule, by mid-November)
Target · December rate at or above 35%, final on January 14

risks.text: Share of calls marked unqualified in the first ten minutes jumps while the rate rises
risks.fix: Amin listens to all of them that week

risks.text: Rate still below 25% four weeks after qualification is locked
risks.fix: Coaching becomes the first priority

risks.text: A December deal flagged as forced, or refunds rising with the rate
risks.fix: Review the cause at the next weekly review, before any new sales initiative (KR 3.3)

krs.name: 3.3 · Refunds within 30 days below 3% of Q4 sales
krs.metric: Sales refunded on a request made within 30 days of payment ÷ sales made in the same period (Oct 1 to Dec 31). A ceiling: at or below 3% is on target
krs.source: Stripe and the refund backlog, every refund logged with its reason the day it is granted · checked by Romain
krs.lead: Share of refunds coming from forced sales

inits.name: Forced sales made visible
inits.hyp: If we log every refund with its reason and define precisely what a forced sale is, then forced sales become visible, coachable and rare
inits.contrib: Refunds from forced sales close to zero

inits.name: First 30 days followed up
inits.hyp: If the Data OS shows every inactive student and every new student is followed up through their first 30 days, then we catch students at risk before they ask for a refund

miles.text: M1 · every refund since Oct 1 logged with its reason in the refund backlog, forced-sale conditions written and validated by the sales team (week to schedule)
M2 · Data OS shows every inactive student and every student in their first 30 days, every flagged student contacted within 24 h (week to schedule, shared with KR 1.3 M2)
October rate final, below 3%
Target · October and November below 3%, December confirmed in January

risks.text: Forced sales explain more than half of refunds four weeks after M1
risks.fix: Sales coaching becomes the first priority, flagged reps’ calls reviewed the following week

risks.text: A refund request from a student the Data OS never flagged
risks.fix: Revise the definition of inactive at the next weekly review

risks.text: A month’s final rate above 3%
risks.fix: Review its root causes at the next weekly review, before any new sales initiative
